findings.finding: The migration-mode chaining mechanism is only safe when Gerrit's commit-msg hook is already installed before `pre-commit install` runs. If a developer (or worktree setup) runs `make hooks`/`make install` first — before fetching the Gerrit hook — pre-commit installs its commit-msg shim with no `.legacy` to chain. Subsequent commits silently receive no Change-Id, breaking every push to Gerrit. The plan mentions empirical verification but does not specify what `make hooks` should do when the Gerrit hook is absent from the commit-msg slot at install time.

scenarios: Developer clones repo and runs `make install` before following the Gerrit hook install step in CONTRIBUTING.md — commit-msg slot gets pre-commit shim with no .legacy chain; commits lack Change-Id.

`make worktree` provisions a new worktree and calls `make install` (which calls `make hooks`) — worktrees share the common hooks dir, so if the parent clone already has both hooks this is fine, but a fresh clone provisioned with `make install` before the Gerrit hook install hits the race.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a guard to `make hooks`: before running `pre-commit install`, check whether `.git/hooks/commit-msg` exists AND is not already a pre-commit shim. If absent, print a clear error directing the user to install the Gerrit hook first (per CONTRIBUTING.md §1b), then exit non-zero. This makes the ordering explicit and detectable rather than silently breaking Change-Id stamping.
